name: DevTools Protocol side effect
plain: A page can notice when a tool is listening to the browser over the DevTools Protocol.
meaning: Playwright, Puppeteer and many cloud browsers drive Chrome through the DevTools Protocol. When the Runtime domain is enabled, the browser serializes logged objects for the tool. A page can plant an Error whose stack getter runs only when that happens, which reveals the listener. Recent tools reduce this, so it is a moving target.

web.api: console.debug(new Error()) with a getter on Error.prototype.stack; any accessor that fires only when Runtime.enable serializes the object

steps: Page defines an Error with a stack getter
Page logs the Error with console.debug
If a protocol client serializes it, the getter runs and the page sees it

chrome.note: Seen with Chromium based browsers driven over the DevTools Protocol

chrome_android.note: Seen when Chrome is driven over the protocol

fields.name: stackGetterCalled
fields.range: true when a protocol client serialized the logged object

limits.headline: Can tell that a debugging tool is attached to the browser
limits.user_action: Nothing. It runs from page script
can: Detect a DevTools Protocol client that enabled the Runtime domain
Add the result to a bot score
Catch automation that hides the webdriver flag
cannot: Work after the tool patches or avoids Runtime.enable
Tell a developer opening DevTools from a bot
limits.reach_label: One yes or no from a side effect
limits.differs: Real developers who open DevTools can trigger it too. Newer automation tools avoid enabling the Runtime domain, which defeats the test.

story.what_it_is: Some tools watch the browser by talking to it behind the scenes. The page can catch that conversation by leaving a trap that only springs when someone listens.

marketing.name: Chrome DevTools Protocol
marketing.pitch: Docs list the protocol domains that tools use to inspect and control Chromium.

story.for_you: You never see it. If you open DevTools yourself it can also fire. Agent tools that use the protocol can be spotted this way.
story.for_makers: This is a cat and mouse game. Treat the result as one weak signal that decays as tools change. Do not use it alone to block people, because opening DevTools can trigger it.

use_cases.example: A bot filter marks sessions where the stack getter fires.
A retailer flags checkout sessions from protocol driven browsers.
An ad verifier removes views from protocol driven browsers.
An anti cheat script looks for a debugger style listener.
A tool maker tests whether their library trips the check.
A fraud team adds the check to a layered score for login attempts.

risks: False positives for people with DevTools open

technical_bounds: Defeated by tools that avoid Runtime.enable
Developers with DevTools open can match

history.change: Runtime.enable serialization described as a way to detect automation
